skill.displayName: Pet Grooming Effectiveness & Hairball Risk Analysis | 宠物梳毛器梳理效果与毛球风险

version.changelog:
- Updated version to 1.0.13.
- SKILL.md updated; version number incremented and documentation improvements.
- Removed redundant file: skill-card.md.
- No changes to features, parameters, or API logic.
- Documentation now more clearly matches skill capabilities and requirements.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly a pet-grooming media analyzer, but it silently creates or reuses service identities, stores reusable tokens, and defaults to insecure HTTP development endpoints.

dimensions.detail: The default common config selects env: dev, which overrides HTTPS service URLs with plaintext HTTP private-network endpoints while requests may carry auth headers, identity fields, and uploaded media.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time hooks, services, or scheduled persistence were found, but one requirements file uses yaml==6.0.3 instead of the expected PyYAML package, creating installation and dependency-resolution risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md discloses server-side API analysis and cloud history, but it uses broad auto-trigger rules, automatic attachment handling, and hidden internal identity handling without a clear per-use consent step for transmitting files, URLs, or history queries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The runtime can silently register/login, create a default local identity, and persist token/openToken values in a plaintext SQLite database under the workspace data directory without secure storage or clear revocation controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main workflow matches remote pet-grooming media analysis and cloud history lookup, but the package also ships broad generic HTTP/CRUD, user lookup, database, and stub agent-chat helpers beyond the narrow grooming purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. Use it only if you are comfortable sending pet/home media, URLs, identity-linked requests, and report history to the publisher's service. The default configuration should be changed to trusted HTTPS production endpoints, and token storage/debug logging should be fixed before normal use.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The broad common modules do contain generic CRUD/list/delete HTTP helpers, user lookup, database utilities, and an AgentSkill stub; most are not directly used by the grooming workflow, but they broaden the shipped capability surface beyond the narrow manifest.
[YR4] unexpected: Manual review of SKILL.md did not confirm hidden instruction text or control-character poisoning; this is downgraded to a metadata hygiene signal rather than a driver of the verdict.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The request path silently calls /sys/phoneLogin with register=1, attaches identity and auth headers, and persists returned token/openToken values; identity association is described, but account creation and credential persistence are under-disclosed.
[LP3] expected: Network access, local file reading, and command invocation are coherent with remote media analysis, but there is no tight permission metadata or host/path allowlist around these capabilities.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading local media or submitting URLs to a server is central to the skill and mentioned in the overview, but the docs do not clearly require user confirmation or explain transmission, retention, or server-side URL fetching.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The manifest sets broad automatic triggers for file/URL analysis and history queries, which can activate cloud processing without an explicit per-run consent step.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-first output is visible throughout the artifact and is not a security issue, though it may affect usability for non-Chinese users.
[SDI-1] expected: History-report listing is declared in SKILL.md, so the capability is not hidden; the concern is that it uses an internal identity path with limited user-visible scoping.
[P9] expected: The whitespace hits match code alignment/formatting in reviewed Python, with no concealed instructions found.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The AgentSkill.ai_chat comments describe subprocess use, but the execution is commented out and the method is not invoked by the grooming script; it is inaccurate dead/stub code, not active agent spawning.
[T09] unexpected: Static evidence is confirmed: the default common config sets env: dev and overrides production HTTPS endpoints with plaintext HTTP 192.168.1.234 endpoints while requests may carry auth headers, identity fields, and media data.
[T09] unexpected: Static evidence is confirmed: reusable token and openToken values are stored as plaintext columns in a SQLite database under the workspace data directory.
[T09] unexpected: Static evidence is partially confirmed: debug mode is enabled in the dev profile and low-level HTTP logging can be enabled, although the helper tries not to print full headers in its own debug statement.
[T08] unexpected: The analysis requirements file declares yaml==6.0.3 while the common component uses PyYAML==6.0.3; this is an install reliability and dependency-confusion risk, not evidence of malicious code.
